subject: general
question: In case of an alternating current, ______.

options.text: the direction of current as well as magnitude changes with time
the direction of current as well as magnitude of current does not change with time
the direction of current changes but magnitude is constant
the direction of current is same but the magnitude changes with time

solution:
The correct answer is **__Option - 1__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points**

__
 
• In alternating current, the electric charge changes direction periodically means the direction varies from instant to instant.
 
• The voltage in the AC circuit also periodically reverses because the current changes direction.
 
• So, a **change in both the direction and magnitude happens.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Alternating current (AC) is a type of electrical current that periodically reverses direction, in contrast to direct current (DC) which flows only in one direction.** 
 
• ***AC is the form in which electric power is delivered to businesses and residences.***
 
• *Alternating current is produced by most power stations and is used in homes and businesses. The AC in most homes and offices has a frequency of 60 hertz, which means it changes direction, or cycles, 60 times each second.*
 
• The advantage of AC is that** it can be transmitted over long distances due to its ability to be easily transformed to high voltage.** High voltage transmission is more efficient because it reduces the energy lost to heat due to the resistance in wires over long distances*. Transformers are used to increase the voltage for transmission and decrease it for user-end applications.*
 
• **Please note** that AC can also be dangerous because it can stop the human heart due to the frequency similar to the heart's electrical signals. Therefore, careful precautions are always taken when working with AC.
